s01.t01:
Subject: Saw your raise, here's a shortcut

Hey [First Name],

Congrats on the Seed round. Saw you're leading your first team at [Company].

We helped another founder in your spot reduce onboarding time by 40% without adding headcount. Happy to share how if you're open to it.

[Your Name]
s01.t02:
Subject: Quick case study, might be useful

Hey [First Name],

Following up. Thought you might find this useful: a breakdown of how we helped [Founder] at [Company] navigate their post-Seed GTM sprint.

Let me know if you'd like the PDF. Happy to send.
s01.t03:
Find B2B SaaS companies founded less than 2 years ago, raised Seed in the past 90 days, are hiring growth roles, use HubSpot, and are led by a first-time founder.

Enrich with job posts, LinkedIn posts, team-size changes, and a summary of recent founder activity.
s01.t05: Urgent to prove traction and likely under-resourced
s01.t07: Cash has landed and growth is expected
s01.t09: Less internal infrastructure and more openness to help
s01.t11: They know they need systems but do not have them yet
s01.t12: Raised Seed or Series A funding in the last 60 to 90 days
s01.t13: Hired a Head of Sales or Marketing
s01.t14: Posted two or more new GTM roles
s01.t15: Launched a product or earned a recent press mention
s01.t16: Founder was promoted or changed titles
s01.t20: See whether the team is expanding
s01.t25: Understand what the founder is discussing
s01.t27: Generate insights and useful first drafts
s01.t33: Stop defining buyers by job title alone. Build prospect lists around pressure, timing, and real buying signals so even a simple message earns attention.

s02.t01: From Tejas Jhaveri, founder to founder
s02.t02: Tejas is a four-time entrepreneur who built Flintstop into a $6M-a-year D2C business before selling it in 2020. At Myntmore, he has helped 130+ B2B companies book 12K+ meetings and generate $120M+ in pipeline. He is also a TEDx speaker and has taught B2B growth methodologies at IIT and IIM.
s02.t03: If your cold emails are not landing, the problem may not be the tool, subject line, or follow-up. It may be who you are sending to.
s02.t04: This framework helps you reach the right people at the right moment. It is the same approach Myntmore uses to help founders book sales conversations without relying on daily posting or broad, volume-heavy outreach.

s03.t01: Redefine your ICP using pressure, not personas
s03.t02: “Marketing manager at a 20 to 500-person SaaS company” tells you who somebody is, but not what they are under pressure to achieve. Go beyond identity and identify the commercial pressure shaping what they care about now.
s03.t03: When your list is full of people under pressure to solve the problem you solve, replies get easier.

s04.t01: Use buying triggers, not job titles
s04.t02: Buyers do not always look like buyers until something changes. That change is your trigger. Triggers turn static lists into real-time context.
s04.t03: “Just saw you raised and hired a Head of Sales. Sounds like you are gearing up GTM. We helped another founder in the same window streamline onboarding before hiring their first reps.”

s05.t01: Turn ICP and triggers into a living prospect list
s05.t02: Smartlead remains Myntmore's go-to sending platform because it is fast, flexible, and built for scale. Clay is not simply a scraping tool. Used well, it becomes the strategy and enrichment layer behind the campaign.

s07.t01: Write emails that feel like timing, not pitching
s07.t02: Send while the trigger is still fresh. Do not overthink surface-level personalisation. Relevance is the real personal touch.

s08.t01: Follow up with credibility, not pressure
s08.t02: If the first message demonstrates timing, the second should demonstrate perspective. Follow-up is not about nagging. It is about returning with something useful and real.

s09.t02: Most founders try to write clever messages. The best build lists so dialled in that a simple, timely note earns a reply. Golden ICP means founder-to-founder empathy at scale.
